x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad, not Kurnool.

s: Under the CCAFS programme of which organisation is the Climate-Smart Village approach promoted?
x: Climate-Smart Village comes under CCAFS of CGIAR; NICRA is the ICAR/CRIDA project.

s: How many climate-resilient crop varieties were released in India during 2014-2025?
x: 2,996 climate-resilient varieties were released in 2014-2025, including heat-tolerant wheat HD 3385.

s: According to FAO-WMO (April 2026), by about how much does extreme heat cut milk yield?
x: Extreme heat cuts milk yield by 15-25%; heat stress sets in above 25°C.

s: In which year did ICAR launch NICRA, led by CRIDA, Hyderabad?
x: NICRA is an ICAR project of 2011, led by CRIDA, Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following is a heat-tolerant wheat variety released in India?
x: HD 3385 is a heat-tolerant wheat variety; the others are rice varieties.

s: What is ACASA-India?
o: A GIS atlas of crop vulnerability to climate change
x: ACASA-India is a GIS-based atlas of crop vulnerability used for climate-resilient agriculture.

s: Which of the following act as protective bio-shields against cyclones in Andhra Pradesh's delta regions?
x: Mangroves and Casuarina shelterbelts protect the delta coast; cyclones damage paddy and aquaculture.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: CWC flood forecasts – Issued at 3,500 stations
Weather-based insurance – Payout when weather crosses specified thresholds
Mangrove and Casuarina shelterbelts – Bio-shields on the Andhra Pradesh coast
x: CWC flood forecasts are issued at 350 stations, not 3,500.

s: The Central Water Commission issues flood forecasts at about how many stations?
x: CWC flood forecasting covers 350 stations, a frequent trap with 3,500.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, an adaptation measure for farmers, launched?
x: PMFBY, India's crop insurance scheme, was launched in 2016.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as an example of which adaptation measure?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as a model of early-warning and preparedness action.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to climate-related risks in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kurnool — sea-level rise caused by polar ice sheets
x: Heat is rising in Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur; Kurnool and Anantapur lie in Rayalaseema, so Rayalaseema–heat stress is the correct pair. Coastal erosion belongs to Uppada (Kakinada), not Palnadu, and the other two pairs give risks that do not fit those places.

s: Which colour-coded alert is correctly matched with its meaning?
x: Orange means be prepared; green means no action, yellow means stay updated and red means take action.

s: When does the India Meteorological Department declare a heat wave on the basis of actual maximum temperature?
o: 42°C, only when the normal maximum is exceeded
x: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature is at least 45°C, regardless of the normal maximum temperature.

s: In which districts of Andhra Pradesh has the increasing frequency and intensity of heat waves been specifically reported?
x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are the Andhra Pradesh districts identified as experiencing increasingly frequent and intense heat waves.

s: The first Heat Action Plan in South Asia was prepared for which city in 2013?
x: Ahmedabad prepared the first Heat Action Plan in South Asia in 2013.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rentachintala — hottest place in Andhra Pradesh
Palnadu — location of the first Heat Action Plan in South Asia
x: Rentachintala in Palnadu is the hottest place in Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are wrong: South Asia's first Heat Action Plan was Ahmedabad's (2013), CRIDA is in Hyderabad and ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad.

s: Why is a wet-bulb temperature of about 35°C considered a critical limit for human survivability?
o: blood circulation stops immediately at that temperature
humidity becomes zero at that temperature
sweat can no longer cool the body effectively above that temperature
the body stops producing sweat below that temperature
x: At a wet-bulb temperature above about 35°C, sweat can no longer cool the body sufficiently, making human survival highly difficult.

s: Which of the following disease-environment relationships is correctly matched?
o: Warmer and wetter conditions — expansion of dengue and malaria
Floods — reduction of cholera and hepatitis
Heat — prevention of heatstroke and cardiovascular strain
x: Warmer and wetter conditions expand dengue and malaria. Floods and heat tend to increase, rather than reduce, the other listed health risks.

s: The APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026 highlights which important feature of heatwaves in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Heatwaves are confined exclusively to the coastal districts
Heatwaves affect only agricultural workers and not urban populations
Heatwaves cause fewer deaths than every other natural hazard in the State
Heatwaves cause more deaths in Andhra Pradesh than any other natural disaster
x: The APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026 identifies heatwaves as causing more deaths in Andhra Pradesh than any other natural disaster.

s: At what relative humidity does wet-bulb temperature equal dry-bulb temperature?
x: At 100% relative humidity no further evaporative cooling is possible, so wet-bulb equals dry-bulb.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated cause or mechanism associated with heat waves in India?
o: Cold ocean currents over the Arabian Sea
The loo over the Gangetic plains
Meandering Rossby waves creating heat domes
x: Meandering Rossby waves and the loo over the Gangetic plains are identified causes. Cold ocean currents over the Arabian Sea are not stated as a cause in this context.

s: The hottest place in Andhra Pradesh, Rentachintala, is in which district?
x: Rentachintala in Palnadu district is AP's hottest place.

s: By what name is the Godavari delta region of Andhra Pradesh known?
x: The Godavari delta is Konaseema; Rayalaseema is the chronically drought-hit interior.

s: Which statement about tropical cyclones and marine heatwaves is correct?
o: The number of marine heatwaves has fallen by half since 1982.
Marine heatwaves can raise cyclone wind speeds by up to 20% and rainfall by up to 12%.
Marine heatwaves reduce the possibility of rapid cyclone intensification.
Cyclones are more frequent in the Arabian Sea than in the Bay of Bengal.
x: Marine heatwaves can increase cyclone wind speeds by up to 20% and rainfall by up to 12%, thereby promoting rapid intensification. Their number has doubled since 1982, and cyclones are more frequent in the Bay of Bengal.

s: In which months do cyclones in Andhra Pradesh, such as Hudhud, Titli and Michaung, generally peak?
x: AP cyclones peak in October-December, hitting North Coastal AP and Nellore/Bapatla hardest.

s: INCOIS prepares Coastal Vulnerability Index maps using how many parameters?
x: INCOIS, Hyderabad, builds Coastal Vulnerability Index maps from 7 parameters.

s: Which of the following is a shoreline erosion hotspot on the Andhra Pradesh coast?
x: Uppada (Kakinada) and the Krishna coast are AP's erosion hotspots.

s: By about how much did the number of cyclones over the Arabian Sea rise between 2001 and 2019?
x: Arabian Sea cyclones rose 52%; very severe cyclones rose 150%.

s: According to NCCR, Chennai, about what share of India's coastline was eroding during 1990-2018?
x: NCCR, Chennai found 33.6% of India's coastline eroding over 1990-2018.

s: In 2025, marine heatwaves affected roughly what share of the world's oceans?
x: Over 90% of oceans saw marine heatwaves in 2025, lowering oxygen and harming fish.

s: What is the length of the coastline of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of about 1,053 km, from Srikakulam to Nellore.

s: Which organisation monitors glacier mass balance and retreat, maps areas vulnerable to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and updates the Himalayan glacier inventory in India?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research
x: The Geological Survey of India performs these monitoring, mapping and inventory-related functions for Himalayan glaciers.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: South Lhonak lake — Sikkim GLOF, October 2023
South Lhonak lake — Nepal flash flood, August 2026
x: The South Lhonak lake GLOF occurred in Sikkim in October 2023. The Chamoli disaster occurred in Uttarakhand in February 2021, while Thame floods occurred in 2024.

s: Where is Himansh, the NCPOR glacier-research station established in 2016, located?
x: Himansh is an NCPOR station above 4,000 m in Lahaul-Spiti, set up in 2016 to study glaciers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about hanging glaciers in the Himalaya?
o: They are tributary glaciers left stranded on steep slopes as valley glaciers thin
Their detachment can cause ice-rock avalanches leading to LLOFs or GLOFs
Rising heat melts the permafrost that anchors them
They form only on valley floors below the permanent snowline
x: Hanging glaciers hang on steep slopes; they do not form on valley floors.

s: Glacier melt in the Himalayas most directly threatens which combination?
o: Only coastal fisheries and mangrove forests
Lean-season river flows and hydropower generation
x: Glacier melt threatens lean-season flows of rivers such as the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and also affects hydropower.

s: Which gases does permafrost thaw in the Himalaya release?
x: Permafrost thaw releases CH4 and CO2 and can damage infrastructure.

s: Where is ICIMOD, which publishes the Hindu Kush Himalaya Snow Update, headquartered?
x: ICIMOD is based in Kathmandu; its 2025 Snow Update found snow persistence 23.6% below normal.

s: The Gangotri glacier has retreated by about how much since 1935?
x: Gangotri has retreated about 1,727 m since 1935, faster in recent years.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zanskar glacier study – Central Water Commission
x: Himansh, NCPOR's station of 2016, is in Lahaul-Spiti; Chamoli is in Uttarakhand, South Lhonak in Sikkim, and the Zanskar study was by IIT Bombay.

s: How many thematic areas does the National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem (NMSHE) have?
x: NMSHE, one of the NAPCC missions, has 12 thematic areas for the Himalaya.

s: Where are the GLOF-prone Gangabal and Nundkol lakes located?
x: Gangabal and Nundkol lakes lie below Harmukh in Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir and are highly GLOF-prone.
